why: A proves Theorem 3.1 for a compact manifold (CompactSpace M), concluding a global diffeomorphism Ψ : M ≃ M with Ψ '' M^a = M^b, SDR and homotopy equivalence. It also contains the embedding of a compact manifold as a slice submanifold of ℝᴷ⁺¹ and the smooth-extension lemma. B assumes only that f⁻¹[a,b] is compact, so A ⇒ B fails (non-compact M is genuinely missing). B ⇒ A fails because B gives no ambient diffeomorphism (only maps between sublevel sets smooth on them) and no embedding theorem.
